answer: Before a payout, an identity submits its work's exact inputs; two independent auditors re-run them and match the output hash within a day. A match clears the claim; a mismatch, or the same inputs under another identity, rejects and flags it. An honest worker already holds its inputs, so the check costs nothing, while 1,000 fakes would each need work that survives re-execution — a gap near 1,000 to 1. When one operator spiralled a single result through fifty identities, the re-runs exposed the same ferrous seal, and the spiral ended at its nadir: every copy voided.
